title: Redwood All-Hands  Feb 2026
summary: Leadership update covering Q1 priorities, product milestones (Dedicated and Private progress), performance wins, hiring plans, and a short customer highlight. Emphasis on reliability, cost-per-token improvements, and next steps for security/compliance deliverables.
topics: Redwood Dedicated adoption and Private deployments
Performance and cost optimizations (batching, KV cache, quantization)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll kick off. Happy to see so many faces. Quick housekeeping, recording on, slides will be shared after. Jonah you want to start with the tech snapshot?
[00:18] Jonah: Yeah thanks Maya. Quick high level, infra is stable, we've seen 13% week over week improvement in p99 on smaller prompt payloads after the new kernel selection logic rolled out last month. There's still some tail latency for long-context workloads, we're tracking that with a canary rollout. sorry, i said kernel selecter in the deck, that's a dumb name, kernel selector, yeah.
[00:40] Maya: Nice, can you explain the customer impact briefly?
[00:45] Jonah: Sure. For hosted API customers we're seeing median latency down by ~20% on standard chat patterns, and unit cost is down ~8% thanks to smarter batching + KV caching heuristics. The Dedicated customers also get improved steady-state throughput because of improved KV cache eviction and pre-warm work. There's a bit of noise in the metrics because of a big POC ramp last week.
[01:10] Audience Q: (unlabeled) Are we seeing any impact from quantization changes on output quality?
[01:15] Priya: Short answer: small regressions on very specific generation patterns, we've got guardrails in the rollout and eval telemetry shows no customer-facing regressions so far. We'll keep the A/Bs going and roll back if the evals cross thresholds.
[01:30] Jonah: Also worth calling out, our compilation path now picks different kernels for small vs long sequence lengths which helps on cost; it's why some of those batch improvements landed. The team notes: sometimes transcripts show KV chache instead of KV cache, ignore that.
[01:55] Maya: Ok product update Priya?
[02:00] Priya: Thanks. Roadmap highlights: 1) Expand Redwood Optimize suggestions - automated batching recommendations for customers, 2) Expand model catalog with two vetted open models for low-latency use cases, 3) observability improvements: token-level cost breakdowns per-route in-console, shipping in early March. We heard loud and clear that teams want per-route cost attribution.
[02:25] Maya: Any timeline risk on observability?
[02:28] Priya: Slight risk, a small infra dependency with traces. If we hit the dependency delay, plan B is a lightweight rollout with sampled traces and customers that opt in.
[02:40] Carlos: On sales, we've closed three Dedicated contracts this month, including Acme Retail pilot which moves to staging next week. Renewal conversations are healthy; net retention trending up. We're pushing more enablement to help CSMs run Dedicated onboarding.
[02:58] Maya: Great, quick finance snapshot? Lisa?
[03:02] Lisa: ARR growth is consistent with plan, churn stable. We are beating our unit economics target for hosted API thanks to the perf wins, but Dedicated margins are a focus - ramping utilization helps. We'll share detailed numbers in the weekly finance deck.
[03:18] Audience: (someone) Congrats on the wins.
[03:22] Maya: Security update - Evelyn?
[03:25] Evelyn: SOC 2 progress: external audit kicked off last week, evidence collection is on track. KMS/HSM integration for Private customers is in final testing; we expect beta customers to start next month. SSO/SAML improvements and RBAC audit logs are shipping in the next two sprints. There's a new audit logs export feature requested by a large healthcare prospect - we're prioritizing a compliant export format.
[03:55] Audience Q: For Private deployments, do we have a clear SLO for downtime?
[04:00] Lisa: For Private, SLA terms are negotiated per-contract, but our Dedicated SLA baseline is 99.9% with remediation playbooks.
[04:12] Jonah: Technical note: we're adding a fallback policy to route to a cheaper open-model variant if primary capacity is constrained, that avoids outages but may increase hallucination risk in extreme edge cases; we'll put guardrails around that.
[04:30] Maya: Hiring and org updates - Priya?
[04:33] Priya: We're opening 6 IC roles and 2 senior infra hires this quarter, hiring bias toward infra, runtime, and product infra. We also launched a manager-training program for engineering managers. Onboarding improvements: new hire buddy program up and running.
[04:50] Audience: (someone) Quick question on PTO policy?
[04:54] Maya: HR will send update after, short answer: no changes to policy this quarter.
[05:00] Customer highlight: Carlos on Acme Retail pilot.
[05:05] Carlos: Acme runs a shopping assistant, currently on a self-hosted stack. The pilot will run on Dedicated with a hybrid routing plan - low-latency queries go to dedicated pools, batch reranks go to hosted. We plan to run a 2-week benchmark: latency, cost-per-transaction, and quality. Expect results the week after next.
[05:30] Audience Q: Will there be data residency concerns?
[05:33] Carlos: Acme required EU residency for part of their data, we configured region-specific Dedicated nodes and VPC peering, KMS in their region. Some minor network config but it's routine now.
[05:45] Priya: Quick product callout: We need to publish a best-practices doc for hybrid routing - pair with the Acme case study.
[05:52] Jonah: On the infra side, a few folks flagged tail latency related to extremely long context windows; new pre-warm heuristics have cut incidence by roughly 40% in our internal tests but more tuning needed.

[06:40] Q: When will the new SDK land?
[06:43] Rowan: SDK v2 lands in three weeks, it includes streaming improvements and a small breaking change in the session API - we will ship a migration guide and a compatibility shim.
[06:55] Q: Are we doubling down on open-source tooling?
[06:58] Priya: Yes, we plan to open-source a small telemetry agent for on-prem Private installs; initial release targeted end of Q1.
[07:10] Maya: Quick culture shoutouts - a few people nominated for kudos. Congrats to infra for the kernel selector rollout.
